method: Blind union of both arms' DELIVERED assertions, built by me from the arms' own documents, not from any runner summary. A proposition enters the union when an arm states it against a cited passage. Classification is mine, against the CURRENT owner text on main - not against the frozen case - and every code or API fact carried by a credited proposition was verified against the arm's own cached source or against the Plans file on main before the proposition was admitted.
assertion_corpus_rule: workspace/notes.md and workspace/leads/*.md only. Excluded as inputs: handoff.md, navigation.md, brief.md, assignment.md, sources.md, tool-help.md, research.py. Excluded as locator inventories: workspace/research-evidence/sources/** (used by me for verification, never as an assertion).
structural_fact: Union propositions can only come from COMPARE-stage documents. I checked every reconcile, discovery, implementation and history note in both arms: all are headed 'external technical reconciliation' or equivalent and NOT ONE cites a Plans/ passage (literal count of 'Plans/' is zero in all 11 reconcile notes and all 13 research notes). So the union rests on FIVE documents: arm-s J0015/J0016/J0017-compare and h2-review J0019/J0020-compare, covering five leads.

findings.title: "A new head" is the wrong staling trigger for Azure
findings.proposition: The staling trigger must be restated as a new PROVIDER REVISION - the provider's own revision identity advancing, OR any leg of (base_revision, head_revision, merge_base_revision) changing. Target-branch movement changes commonRefCommit and therefore revision identity while producing no iteration and no head change, so the Plans are internally inconsistent: identity is a triple and the staling trigger is one leg of it.
findings.provider_evidence: IterationReason publishes exactly seven values (push, forcePush, create, rebase, unknown, retarget, resolveConflicts) with an empty Description for every one; retarget carries newTargetRefName/oldTargetRefName and moves no head; commonRefCommit is defined by BOTH refs.

my_source_verification.finding: IterationReason publishes exactly seven values - push, forcePush, create, rebase, unknown, retarget, resolveConflicts - with an EMPTY Description column for every one. Verified in arm-s J0015-compare research-evidence/sources/S00039/text.txt lines 468-479.

GitPullRequestIteration carries sourceRefCommit ('The source Git commit of this iteration'), targetRefCommit ('The target Git commit of this iteration') and commonRefCommit ('The first common Git commit of the source and target refs'). Verified in arm-s J0015 S00039/text.txt lines 259-261, 288-293.

findings.promise_served: P1 never show stale review evidence as current
findings.contradiction_exposed: ADO-003 makes revision identity a TRIPLE (base, head, merge-base) and makes the staling trigger ONE LEG of it, so a revision's own identity fields can change with no head change and no new iteration - internally inconsistent inside the frozen Plans.

findings.title: An unmapped provider revision cause must never render as a push
findings.proposition: The provider's stated cause is persisted VERBATIM as a raw wire string alongside the typed one. A cause PM cannot map renders as unknown cause, never as push. Microsoft's own shipped client collapses any unrecognised reason to Push because IterationReason.Push = 0 and the accumulator guard is `if (resultPart)`.
findings.provider_evidence: azure-devops-node-api@af336d2 api/Serialization.ts:262-295; the REST reference publishes seven single names with empty descriptions while the client enum is bit-valued.
findings.contradiction_exposed: The provider publishes seven causes with empty descriptions and the reference implementation collapses anything unrecognised to `push`, the most reassuring value; nothing in the Plans forbids PM doing the same.

findings.title: A retarget invalidates the applicable policy SET, not only the evidence
findings.proposition: Because branch policies are configured per target ref, a retarget changes WHICH policies apply at all: previously-satisfied required reviewers may cease to be required and new ones may appear. The repair re-resolves the policy/check set rather than carrying it.

findings.contradiction_exposed: Policies are scoped to the target ref, so a retarget changes WHICH policies apply; ADO-003 stales only the evidence and says nothing about the applicable set.

findings.proposition: review_revision.evidence_state is a closed four-value enum in which only stale_head_changed names a cause, so at least five distinct Azure staleness causes (retarget, merge-base drift from target movement, web-UI conflict resolution, force push, policy-driven time expiry) would all be reported to the person as 'head changed' - false in four of the five, and in contradiction with ADO-003's own negative constraint against flattening.

findings.proposition: Truncation is a distinct axis from staleness and the revision object has no room for it. Four truncation conventions sit on one Azure path (hasMoreCommits, commitTooManyChanges, commentTruncated, and $top/$skip with nextSkip/nextTop on the changes route), and review_revision is additionalProperties:false with no completeness field, so evidence can be shown as current while being partial - the brief's own failure mode reached with no staleness at all.

The corpus already knows how to express a revision pair - command_target requires left_review_revision_ref AND right_review_revision_ref for review.version.compare - and simply does not extend it to threads. Created-at and tracked-to must be two separate facts, 'no tracking record' a third state, and a partial anchor tuple must never be persisted.

findings.title: policy_scope_missing is a read-side reason the Azure service cannot produce
findings.proposition: Azure DevOps has no read-side policy permission: the Git Repositories namespace's policy bits (EditPolicies, PolicyExempt, PullRequestBypassPolicy) are all write/exempt/bypass, and reading policies rides on repository GenericRead - the evaluations endpoint lists exactly one OAuth scope, vso.code, the same scope that reads code. So 'I can see this repository but not its branch policies' is not a state the service has, and a caller who got policy_scope_missing would have been denied at the repository. ADO-002's distinguishability promise is real for the WRITE and BYPASS paths and the plan does not say which it means.
findings.provider_evidence: Security-namespace reference (Git Repositories namespace policy bits) plus the evaluations endpoint's single vso.code scope.
findings.contradiction_exposed: ADO-002 promises policy access failures stay distinguishable and the Services fixture declares policy_scope_missing, but Azure has no read-side policy permission - the state cannot be produced on the read path.

findings.title: Nothing in the corpus forbids client-side policy scope resolution
findings.proposition: The Plans constrain the OUTPUT of the policy mapping ('without losing policy identity') and say nothing about the DERIVATION. No statement requires provider-side applicability resolution, no prohibition on client-side scope resolution exists, and policy scope levels, matchKind and refName matching appear nowhere. An implementer who reads only the Plans, reaches for the obvious-looking collection endpoint and filters it client-side has violated no written constraint and produces a confident single WRONG answer, not an error - so no reason code fires and 'partial data is never complete' never gets a chance to apply. The corpus already has the right shape in an unrelated owner: FileSafe.md:225's fail-closed-on-scope-resolution rule.

findings.title: A check item must declare HOW its status is bound to a revision
findings.proposition: Three admissible bindings: revision_bound (the provider keyed the status by commit - Azure Git statuses, and the released per-iteration statuses route), review_bound (keyed by review only - Azure policy evaluations; the record carries the head the provider reported in the same transaction plus a head_matched_request flag), and unbound. When the heads do not match the item is review_revision_stale, not failed and not unknown, and the whole batch is not silently re-bound to the new head. findings.title: cmd.forge.review.merge carries no merge strategy, and omitting one is not neutral
findings.proposition: The obvious reading of the frozen Plans is that the product cannot have the reported bug because the merge command has no merge-strategy field at all and 'merge strategy' in Azure's sense appears nowhere in the corpus. That reading is wrong: omitting MergeStrategy is not neutral - 'If MergeStrategy is not set to any value, a no-FF merge will be created if SquashMerge == false', noFastForward is the default, and Microsoft recommends setting it explicitly in all cases. So a strategy-less completion is a noFastForward completion, and if the repository policy forbids no-fast-forward the request is refused. The product lands in the same place by the opposite route: the reported tool CHOOSES a strategy and can choose wrongly; the Plans as frozen choose one implicitly and cannot choose at all. Even a product that never displays a branch policy must know which merge strategies the effective policy permits the moment it offers a merge button.

Enforcement is in the schema, not only in prose: project is a required key of repository_locator and the azure_devops branch narrows it to a non-empty string, with a matching negative fixture.

findings.provider_evidence: The Plans forbid precisely the defect that shipped in a real Azure module.

findings.title: Different kinds of 'no' stay different
findings.proposition: ADO-002 keeps authentication method, account, organization/collection access, project access, repository access, branch-policy scope, build/pipeline access, API compatibility, rate and readiness distinct, and requires typed limits and remediation; capability_entry carries requested and effective as separate booleans and availability_payload requires state plus reason_codes plus allowed_action_ids.

findings.title: Provider-native status round-trips without flattening at the storage layer
findings.proposition: SCS-016 requires provider-neutral projections to materialize Check with raw AND normalized status, exact revision, canonical URL, native object vocabulary and preserved vendor extensions, and vendor_extensions_preserved is a const true - so a record that drops extensions cannot validate. The wire value 'broken' is REQUIRED to survive into raw_status and the opaque context blob has a lawful home. Covered for round-trip; the rendering layer is a separate gap.

my_source_verification.finding: source_control_contracts.schema.json on main: normalized_remote_record requires canonical_url (type string, format uri) and revision_ref; record_kind includes Check; raw_status and normalized_status are unconstrained strings with minLength 1. VERIFIED.

findings.title: API versions and feature availability are signed catalog/probe data, not constants
findings.proposition: §7 states it for Server versions, APIs, auth methods, access rules, tiers/licenses and feature availability; ADO-002 requires a current signed host/version support entry and fails Server mutation closed without one. The cloud-only scope of a provider documentation page is therefore a data-acquisition problem the Plans already anticipate, not a Plan defect.

findings.title: Real progress, no spinner-as-result
findings.proposition: ADO-004 requires ObservableWork and terminal provider receipts and forbids inferring progress from time; FGI-005 makes run/retry/cancel asynchronous guarded work with one terminal provider result; the schema adds external_effect_reconciliation with successful_cli_exit_proves_remote_state const false and accepted_request_distinct_from_durable_outcome const true. A queued or running policy evaluation is an in-progress fact and the Plans already forbid presenting acceptance as completion.

findings.title: 'May I read branch policies' is already a distinct five-state administrative fact
findings.proposition: hosted_administration_surface enumerates repository_policy and branch_policy as separate areas, each with an independent read_state (ready, permission_denied, unsupported, external_only, unknown) and write_state. unknown as a first-class read state is exactly what distinguishing '200 empty', 'this host cannot answer' and 'not allowed to read' needs. Covered for the Settings administration surface; it is not wired to the per-pull-request checks list.

findings.title: A checks query must bind an exact head OID from a current projection
findings.proposition: The command conditional pins requested_capability const checks, currentness.state const current, identity_source const validated_repository_binding, target_kind const review_checks, and requires provider_review_id and review_head_oid with a hex pattern - with a positive fixture and a negative fixture whose expected error is 'check projection must bind the exact review head OID'. So the Plans already forbid a checks list fetched by PR number alone and one fetched from a stale projection. The residual gap is about WHICH commits, not whether a commit.

findings.title: 'Unknown is not passing' is already a rule, a vocabulary and an acceptance scenario
findings.proposition: SCS-015's negative constraint forbids turning unavailable or unknown checks into zero failed checks or unsupported; the availability vocabulary is explicit and 'unknown is never flattened to unsupported'; acceptance scenario E2E-015 'Unknown checks are not passing checks' exists. This lines up exactly with the provider's pending / notSet blocking-awaiting-result and with queued / running evaluations.

findings.title: Cloud and Server separation is structurally enforced
findings.proposition: The variant enum is closed and enforced by a schema conditional on provider == azure_devops; separate adapter profiles exist with different auth methods, container kinds, gates and reason codes.

findings.title: On Server the evaluations surface exists, is preview and is collection-addressed
findings.proposition: Microsoft publishes a separate on-prem swagger for the policy area whose route templates are /{collection}/{project}/_apis/policy/evaluations carrying x-ms-preview true, an override version of 7.1-preview.1 and oauth2 [vso.code]. So the older parent question 'which policy APIs are MISSING on Server' has the answer 'none missing - the available api-version surface differs', confirmed from a machine-readable artifact.
findings.provider_evidence: policy/azure-devops-server-7.1/policy-onprem.json, 38,733 bytes, blob sha a9c40e117edeff0dfbc46df5c1e6242d15bbc9ce.

findings.title: A connection must not be derived from the origin remote
findings.proposition: The predecessor read .git/config, took remote 'origin' and classified by substring, with its own header comment admitting the on-prem arm 'is basically a catch all. Any url could match it'. The Plans already make the remote non-load-bearing: hierarchy may not be inferred from a URL or focused view, migration cannot invent project or authority from a remote URL, and saved hosting bindings rather than a remote named origin choose among fork/upstream/multi-forge routes.
findings.provider_evidence: The successor product converged on the Plans' position, requiring explicit org and project settings with remote inference as a narrow fallback - and its own inference regex still fails for the plain dev.azure.com form.

findings.title: Activation preconditions must stay distinguishable from authentication failure
findings.proposition: A closed issue reported as 'unable to configure PAT' was not a credential problem at all - the extension never activated because no repository folder was open. capability_entry's separate requested and effective booleans and availability_payload's state plus reason_codes plus allowed_action_ids already distinguish 'cannot authenticate' from 'never attempted'.

findings.title: An SSH remote is not an API connection, and an auth method is never readiness by itself
findings.proposition: ADO-002's acceptance is explicit: 'Entra/PAT/SSH are auth methods or refs, never readiness by themselves', and authentication may not be equated with project or repository access.

findings.title: A thin PR surface with browser delegation is already addressed
findings.proposition: The common review contract and the fallback ladder already own what a review surface must show and what it may delegate.
owner_passages_cited: Forge_Integrations.md (reviews, GUI section grammar and fallback ladder)

findings.title: Hand-built provider URLs from an unvalidated remote are already forbidden
findings.proposition: Display URLs and local paths remain descriptive only; hierarchy may not be inferred from a URL; URL parsing is discovery evidence only.

findings.title: Polling cost and silent polling failure are already covered by typed availability and currentness
findings.proposition: One glyph for every kind of 'no' is precisely what the typed availability vocabulary, reason codes and currentness states exist to prevent.

findings.title: Stale evidence presented as current is already forbidden
findings.proposition: The immutable review revision, evidence_state, currentness and the 'evidence currentness' clause of ADO-003 already forbid it.

findings.title: Capability verdicts must not be synthesised from an error string
findings.proposition: §7 forbids terminal prose scraping and FGI-003 requires capability resolution from a capability entry, not from an error body. The predecessor inferred an unsupported repository kind from an authorization error and misdiagnosed in both directions.

findings.title: On-prem transport trust is already covered by FGI-015's instance-trust requirements
findings.proposition: FGI-015 requires instance trust to validate normalized host, tenant/account, API base path, scoped private CA, redirects/pagination, SSH host key and explicit localhost/metadata policy BEFORE credentials - which is what a TLS-verification bypass violates.

findings.title: Credential custody and key scoping are already covered
findings.proposition: Secrets remain credential refs, raw credentials may not be persisted, and Settings shows access and currentness without raw credentials.

findings.title: Adjacent products are optional capability projections, not implied by repository access
findings.proposition: §7: 'Boards/issues are optional capability projections and are not silently claimed by repository access.'
